known_limitations: Circular lunar orbit is assumed kinematic and is not stability-validated.
Receiver capture uses a uniform paraxial solar disc, a projected-area-equivalent circular receiver, and midpoint integration over the rectangular mirror aperture.
Diffraction, solar limb darkening, mirror surface slope errors, structural occlusion, and thermal behavior are not modeled.
Terrain horizons are local and limited range; absent or incomplete terrain leaves visibility unknown.
Pointing-offset lateral beam overlap is not modeled; nonzero pointing error must remain unknown.
Successful model energy accounting is not evidence of operational or real lunar mission feasibility.

provenance.calculation_engine: existing core.lumen simulation and validation APIs
provenance.emergency_recovery_capture_model: shared core.lumen.lumen_receiver receiver result; no bounding-circle fallback
provenance.orbit: assumed kinematic circular orbit; not SPICE-propagated or stability-validated
provenance.receiver_capture_model: core.lumen.lumen_receiver.calculate_receiver_power; finite solar disc and rectangular mirror aperture midpoint integration
provenance.terrain: synthetic test horizon only; real site terrain is UNKNOWN
provenance.time_and_geometry: deterministic synthetic demo provider; no SPICE kernels queried

unknown_evidence: No measured or authoritative lunar-site illumination data is included.
No measured terrain profile is included; synthetic clear horizons exercise code paths only.
No operational orbital perturbation/stability analysis is included.
Hardware performance, reflector pointing, thermal behavior, and mission operations are unvalidated.
Operational mission feasibility remains UNKNOWN even when the synthetic calculation ledger passes.
